Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১) Which organelle is responsible for exportable protein synthesis?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) is responsible for the synthesis of exportable/secretory proteins. Ribosomes attached to the RER synthesize proteins that enter the ER lumen, where they undergo initial folding and processing before being transported to the Golgi apparatus for further modification and packaging.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • RER → secretory/exportable proteins ⭐

  • Free ribosomes → cytosolic proteins

  • Golgi → modification, sorting & packaging

  • Lysosome → intracellular digestion

Exam Pearl:
Export protein → RER → Golgi → secretory vesicle → outside cell.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২) Which of the following serves to cushion and insulate the skin and other organs?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Adipocytes are specialized cells that store fat (triglycerides) and are the main cells of adipose tissue. Adipose tissue provides cushioning and insulation, protects internal organs from mechanical injury, and serves as an important energy reserve.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adipocyte → fat storage + cushioning + insulation 

  • Fibroblast → produces collagen and extracellular matrix

  • Histiocyte/macrophage → phagocytosis and immune defense

  • Adipose tissue → energy storage + thermal insulation

Exam Pearl:
Adipocyte = insulation + cushioning + energy storage.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩) What is the lining epithelium of thyroid?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The thyroid gland follicles are lined by simple cuboidal epithelium. The follicular cells synthesize and secrete thyroid hormones (T3 and T4), which are stored in the follicular colloid as thyroglobulin.

The height of follicular cells can vary with functional activity:

  • Inactive thyroid → flattened/low cuboidal cells

  • Active thyroid → taller cuboidal to columnar cells

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thyroid follicles → Simple cuboidal epithelium 

  • Colloid → contains thyroglobulin

  • Follicular cells → T3 & T4

  • Parafollicular (C) cells → Calcitonin

Exam Pearl:
Thyroid follicle = simple cuboidal epithelium + colloid.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪) What is the content of lacunae?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A lacuna is a small cavity within the bone matrix that contains an osteocyte, the mature bone cell. Osteocytes maintain the surrounding bone matrix and communicate through tiny channels called canaliculi.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Lacuna → Osteocyte ⭐

  • Osteoblast → bone-forming cell

  • Osteoclast → bone-resorbing cell

  • Osteoprogenitor cell → precursor of osteoblasts

Exam Pearl:
“Osteocyte lives in lacuna; osteoblast builds; osteoclast breaks.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫) Venae comitantes are especially found in.......?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Venae comitantes are paired deep veins that accompany an artery, especially in the extremities. They are commonly seen with medium-sized arteries and are connected by transverse communicating channels. Pulsations of the accompanying artery help promote venous return.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Venae comitantes → paired veins accompanying arteries

  • Especially common → extremities 

  • Help venous return through the musculovenous pump + arterial pulsations

  • Large arteries generally have single accompanying veins

Exam Pearl:
“Venae comitantes = companion veins of arteries, especially in limbs.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬) Atherosclerosis occurs in........?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Atherosclerosis primarily affects the tunica intima of medium- and large-sized arteries. Lipid accumulation, inflammatory cells, and fibrous tissue form an atheromatous plaque within the intima, which can progressively narrow the arterial lumen.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Atherosclerosis → Tunica intima 

  • Atheromatous plaque → intimal lesion

  • Commonly affects → large and medium arteries

  • Plaque complications → thrombosis, rupture, stenosis

Exam Pearl:
Atherosclerosis = intimal disease.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭) Human vision is......?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Humans have binocular vision, meaning both eyes work together to provide a combined visual field. The overlapping visual fields of the two eyes allow the brain to perceive depth and three-dimensional (3D) vision.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Human vision → Binocular 

  • Two eyes contribute → depth perception

  • Binocular vision → stereoscopic/3D vision

  • Uniocular → vision using one eye

Exam Pearl:
Two eyes + overlapping visual fields = binocular vision.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮) Motion sickness is due to excessive and repeated stimulation of.......?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Motion sickness occurs mainly due to excessive or repeated stimulation of the vestibular apparatus, particularly when there is a mismatch between information received from the vestibular system, eyes, and proprioceptors. This commonly occurs during travel by car, ship, or aircraft.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Motion sickness → Vestibular apparatus 

  • Main receptors → semicircular canals + otolith organs

  • Trigger → sensory mismatch

  • Symptoms → nausea, vomiting, dizziness, sweating

Exam Pearl:
Motion sickness = vestibular stimulation + sensory conflict.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯) Which is a superficial reflex?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The plantar reflex is a superficial cutaneous reflex. It is elicited by stroking the lateral border of the sole, normally producing plantar flexion of the toes.

The other options are deep tendon/periosteal reflexes:

  • Ankle jerk → deep tendon reflex

  • Finger flexion reflex → deep reflex

  • Radial periosteal reflex → deep periosteal reflex

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Superficial reflex → Plantar reflex 

  • Deep reflexes → biceps, triceps, supinator, knee, ankle

  • Plantar reflex → S1–S2

  • Extensor plantar/Babinski → corticospinal tract lesion in adults

Exam Pearl:
Plantar reflex is the classic superficial reflex tested clinically.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০) Which is the process of uptake of dissolved substances?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pinocytosis is the process by which a cell takes up extracellular fluid and dissolved substances through the formation of small vesicles. It is often called “cell drinking.”

  • Pinocytosis → uptake of fluids and dissolved substances

  • Phagocytosis → uptake of large solid particles (“cell eating”)

  • Endocytosis → general term including pinocytosis and phagocytosis

  • Exocytosis → release of substances from the cell

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Dissolved substances/fluid → Pinocytosis 

  • Solid particles → Phagocytosis

  • Both → Endocytosis

  • Release outside cell → Exocytosis

Exam Pearl:
Pino = “drink” → Pinocytosis = cell drinking.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১১) Which one is direct cell division?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Amitosis is known as direct cell division because the nucleus divides directly by constriction, without spindle formation or the distinct stages of mitosis.

  • Amitosis → direct cell division

  • Mitosis → indirect/equational division with spindle formation

  • Meiosis → reduction division

  • Cytokinesis → division of the cytoplasm, not nuclear division

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Direct cell division → Amitosis 

  • Indirect cell division → Mitosis

  • Reduction division → Meiosis

  • Cytokinesis → cytoplasmic division

Exam Pearl:
Amitosis = direct division without spindle formation.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১২) Sebaceous glands and sweat glands present in which layer of skin?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Sebaceous glands and sweat glands are skin appendages located mainly in the reticular layer of the dermis. Their ducts may extend toward the epidermis, but the glandular portions are embedded in the deeper dermis.

  • Epidermis → no glands

  • Papillary dermis → superficial, mainly loose connective tissue

  • Reticular dermis → contains hair follicles, sebaceous glands, and sweat glands

  • Subcutaneous tissue → mainly adipose tissue

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Sebaceous gland → reticular dermis

  • Sweat gland → reticular dermis

  • Hair follicle → reticular dermis

  • Epidermis → avascular

Exam Pearl:
Skin appendages are mainly located in the reticular layer of the dermis.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৩) What is the dermatome of umbilicus?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The umbilicus corresponds to the T10 dermatome. This is a classic anatomical landmark used when assessing sensory levels in neurological examination.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • T4 → Nipple

  • T6 → Xiphisternum

  • T10 → Umbilicus 

  • L1 → Inguinal region

Exam Pearl:
“T10 = umbilicus.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৪) Which neuroglial cell provides structural support and organization to the central nervous system?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Astrocytes are the major supporting glial cells of the central nervous system (CNS). They provide structural support and organization, help maintain the extracellular environment, contribute to the blood–brain barrier, regulate ions and neurotransmitters, and support neuronal metabolism.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Astrocyte → structural & metabolic support of CNS 

  • Oligodendrocyte → myelin formation in CNS

  • Ependymal cell → lines ventricles and central canal

  • Satellite cell → support cells in the PNS

Exam Pearl:
Astrocytes = “supporting framework” of the CNS.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৫) Which one is the deepest layer of skin epidermis?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The stratum basale (stratum germinativum) is the deepest layer of the epidermis, lying directly on the basement membrane above the dermis. It contains actively dividing basal keratinocytes, melanocytes, and Merkel cells.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Deepest → Stratum basale

  • Then → Spinosum → Granulosum → Lucidum* → Corneum

  • Basale → continuous cell division

  • Melanocytes → located in stratum basale

*Stratum lucidum is present only in thick skin.

Exam Pearl:
“Basale = base = deepest epidermal layer.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৬) Which type of capillaries are most common?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Continuous capillaries are the most common type of capillary in the body. They have an uninterrupted endothelial lining and continuous basement membrane, allowing relatively selective exchange of substances.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Continuous → most common 

  • Fenestrated → kidney, endocrine glands, intestinal mucosa

  • Fenestrated without diaphragm → renal glomeruli

  • Discontinuous/sinusoidal → liver, spleen, bone marrow

Exam Pearl:
Continuous capillaries are the commonest capillaries in the body.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৭) Melanocyte stimulating hormone (MSH) is produced from.....?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) is classically produced by the pars intermedia of the anterior pituitary. It is derived from the POMC (proopiomelanocortin) precursor and stimulates melanocytes to increase melanin production.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pars intermedia → MSH 

  • Pars distalis → ACTH, TSH, GH, FSH, LH, prolactin

  • Pars tuberalis → part of adenohypophysis surrounding the infundibulum

  • MSH → promotes melanin production

Exam Pearl:
Pars intermedia = MSH.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৮) Which is true end artery?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The central retinal artery is a classic example of a true (anatomical) end artery. It has essentially no significant anastomoses, so obstruction can cause sudden and severe retinal ischemia and vision loss.

  • Central retinal artery → true end artery 

  • Coronary artery → functional end arteries

  • Splenic artery → has collateral/anastomotic circulation

  • Carotid artery → not a true end artery

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • True end artery → Central retinal artery

  • Functional end arteries → coronary arteries

  • Occlusion of retinal artery → severe visual loss

Exam Pearl:
Central retinal artery = classic true end artery.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১৯) The adrenal gland lacks.......?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The adrenal (suprarenal) glands lack a true hilum. Unlike many other organs, their blood vessels enter through multiple points on the gland rather than through a single hilum. They have a fibrous capsule, a rich blood supply, and supporting connective tissue.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adrenal gland → no true hilum 

  • Has → fibrous capsule

  • Has → very rich blood supply

  • Located → superior to kidneys

  • Cortex → steroid hormones

  • Medulla → catecholamines

Exam Pearl:
Adrenal gland = richly vascularized but lacks a true hilum.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২০) Which valve is present in between left atrium & left ventricle?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The mitral (bicuspid) valve is located between the left atrium and left ventricle. It prevents backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium during ventricular systole.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Left atrium → left ventricle → Mitral valve 

  • Right atrium → right ventricle → Tricuspid valve

  • Left ventricle → aorta → Aortic valve

  • Right ventricle → pulmonary trunk → Pulmonary valve

Exam Pearl:
“Left = Mitral, Right = Tricuspid.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২১) Which is not one of the major targets of PTH?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The bile duct is not a target of parathyroid hormone (PTH). The major target organs of PTH are bone and kidney. PTH acts on osteoblasts to increase RANKL expression, indirectly stimulating osteoclast-mediated bone resorption. In the kidney, it increases calcium reabsorption and decreases phosphate reabsorption. PTH also indirectly increases intestinal calcium absorption by stimulating renal activation of vitamin D (calcitriol).

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PTH → Bone 

  • PTH → Renal tubules 

  • PTH → Intestine indirectly via calcitrioL

Exam Pearl:
PTH: ↑Ca²⁺, ↓phosphate → bone + kidney; intestine indirectly.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২২) Centroacinar cells that is unique to.........?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Centroacinar cells are a characteristic and unique histological feature of the exocrine pancreas. They represent the beginning of the intercalated ducts, with their cells appearing to extend into the center of the pancreatic acinus.

They are involved in secreting the aqueous, bicarbonate-rich pancreatic juice.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Centroacinar cells → Pancreas 

  • Pancreas → serous acini + centroacinar cells

  • Intercalated ducts → begin within pancreatic acini

  • Salivary glands → do not have centroacinar cells

Exam Pearl:
“Centroacinar = pancreas.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৩) Which one is secret by delta cell of pancreas?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The delta (δ) cells of the pancreatic islets secrete somatostatin. Somatostatin inhibits the secretion of several gastrointestinal and pancreatic hormones, including insulin and glucagon.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • β-cells → Insulin 

  • α-cells → Glucagon

  • δ-cells → Somatostatin

  • PP/F cells → Pancreatic polypeptide

Exam Pearl:
“Alpha = Glucagon, Beta = Insulin, Delta = Somatostatin.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৪) Which one is not the content of portal triad??
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The portal triad consists of three structures within the portal tract:

  • Portal vein → branch

  • Hepatic artery → branch

  • Bile duct/ductule → branch

The hepatic vein is not part of the portal triad. Hepatic veins drain blood from the liver into the inferior vena cava.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Portal triad → Portal vein + Hepatic artery + Bile duct 

  • Hepatic vein → NOT part of portal triad

  • Portal vein → brings nutrient-rich blood to liver

  • Hepatic artery → supplies oxygenated blood

Exam Pearl:
“Portal triad = 2 vessels + 1 duct; hepatic vein is excluded.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৫) Which is not a retroperitoneal organ?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The stomach is an intraperitoneal organ, not retroperitoneal. It is almost completely covered by visceral peritoneum and is suspended by peritoneal ligaments.

The kidneys, pancreas (except its tail), and abdominal aorta are retroperitoneal structures.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Kidney → Retroperitoneal 

  • Pancreas → Retroperitoneal (tail is intraperitoneal)

  • Aorta → Retroperitoneal

  • Stomach → Intraperitoneal 

Exam Pearl:
“SAD PUCKER” helps recall retroperitoneal organs; stomach is not one of them.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৬) What is the basis of axial skeleton?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The notochord forms the embryological axial support/basis of the developing axial skeleton. It establishes the primitive midline axis of the embryo and plays an important role in inducing and organizing surrounding tissues, particularly the paraxial mesoderm that forms the vertebral column.

In adults, most of the notochord disappears, persisting mainly as the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral discs.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Notochord → basis of axial skeleton ⭐

  • Notochord → induces neural tube formation

  • Notochord remnant → nucleus pulposus

  • Vertebrae → derived mainly from sclerotome

Exam Pearl:
Notochord = primitive axial skeleton/supporting rod.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৭) What is sometimes called third testis?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The prostate gland is sometimes referred to as the “third testis” because of its important role in male reproductive function and its contribution to seminal fluid.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Prostate → sometimes called “third testis” 

  • Epididymis → sperm maturation and storage

  • Seminal vesicle → fructose-rich seminal fluid

  • Urethra → passage for urine and semen

Exam Pearl:
Third testis = Prostate gland.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৮) Which of the following is most important ICF electrolyte in excess?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Potassium (K⁺) is the major intracellular fluid (ICF) cation. Its concentration inside cells is much higher than in extracellular fluid (ECF), making it the most important ICF electrolyte in excess.

  • K⁺ → major ICF cation 

  • Na⁺ → major ECF cation

  • Cl⁻ → major ECF anion

  • HCO₃⁻ → important ECF anion

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ICF → K⁺, Mg²⁺, phosphate, proteins

  • ECF → Na⁺, Cl⁻, HCO₃⁻

  • Na⁺ → main determinant of ECF volume

  • K⁺ → main determinant of resting membrane potential

Exam Pearl:
“K⁺ is inside; Na⁺ is outside.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ২৯) Which of the following can cause hemolysis?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Copper toxicity can cause intravascular hemolysis, particularly in acute copper poisoning. Excess copper produces oxidative damage to the RBC membrane, leading to hemolysis. A classic example is Wilson disease, where acute hepatic copper release can cause Coombs-negative intravascular hemolytic anemia.

  • Copper → hemolysis 

  • Lead → classically causes inhibition of heme synthesis and basophilic stippling

  • Zinc → excessive zinc can cause copper deficiency, but is not the classic direct hemolytic toxin

  • Chromium → not a classic cause of hemolysis in standard exam questions

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Copper toxicity → hemolysis

  • Wilson disease → Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia

  • Lead → basophilic stippling + abdominal pain + neuropathy

  • Copper excess → oxidative RBC injury

Exam Pearl:
Wilson disease + acute hemolysis = think copper.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩০) Which one is the first line defense against infection?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the given options, neutrophils are considered the first-line cellular defense against infection, especially acute bacterial infections. They are rapidly recruited to sites of infection and destroy pathogens by phagocytosis, degranulation, and oxidative killing.

  • Neutrophil → first-line cellular defense 

  • Macrophage → important resident phagocyte and innate immune defense

  • Lymphocyte → adaptive immune response

  • Basophil → mainly involved in allergic and inflammatory responses

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute bacterial infection → Neutrophils

  • First responders → Neutrophils

  • Adaptive immunity → Lymphocytes

  • Phagocytosis → Neutrophils + macrophages

Exam Pearl:
Neutrophils are the first cellular responders to acute infection.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩১) Confirmatory test for diagnosis of iron deficiency anemia does not include---?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A peripheral blood film (PBF) is useful for suggesting iron deficiency anemia by showing microcytic, hypochromic RBCs, anisocytosis, and pencil cells, but it is not a confirmatory test for iron deficiency.

Iron studies provide confirmation:

  • Serum ferritin ↓ → most useful/specific indicator of depleted iron stores

  • Serum iron ↓

  • TIBC ↑

  • Transferrin saturation ↓

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • IDA → Ferritin ↓ 

  • Serum iron → ↓

  • TIBC → ↑

  • Transferrin saturation → ↓

  • PBF → microcytic, hypochromic picture

Exam Pearl:
PBF suggests IDA; iron studies—especially low ferritin—confirm it.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩২) Bleeding time is prolonged in -----?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Bleeding time (BT) assesses primary hemostasis, mainly platelet function and platelet–vessel wall interaction. In von Willebrand disease (vWD), deficiency or dysfunction of von Willebrand factor (vWF) impairs platelet adhesion, causing prolonged bleeding time.

In hemophilia, platelet function is normal, so BT is typically normal; the aPTT is prolonged because hemophilia is a coagulation-factor disorder.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • vWD → BT ↑, aPTT may ↑ ⭐

  • Hemophilia → BT normal, aPTT ↑

  • Platelet disorders → BT ↑

  • PT → extrinsic pathway

  • aPTT → intrinsic pathway

Exam Pearl:
“vWD = prolonged bleeding time; Hemophilia = prolonged aPTT.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৩) What is not a features of hypovolemic shock?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Bradypnea (slow breathing) is not a typical feature of hypovolemic shock. Hypovolemia causes reduced circulating volume and tissue perfusion, triggering sympathetic compensation with tachycardia, hypotension, and tachypnea.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypovolemic shock → Hypotension ⭐

  • → Tachycardia ⭐

  • → Tachypnea ⭐

  • → Cold, clammy skin

  • → Reduced urine output

  • Bradypnea → Not typical

Exam Pearl:
Shock generally produces “fast” compensatory responses: fast pulse + fast breathing.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৪) What is cause of QRS complex?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarization, which electrically initiates ventricular contraction (ventricular systole). Strictly speaking, QRS itself is not the mechanical systole; it is the electrical event that precedes and triggers it.

  • P wave → atrial depolarization → atrial systole

  • QRS complex → ventricular depolarization → ventricular systole 

  • T wave → ventricular repolarization → ventricular diastole

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • P → Atrial depolarization

  • QRS → Ventricular depolarization

  • T → Ventricular repolarization

Exam Pearl:
QRS = ventricular depolarization, followed by ventricular systole.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৫) What is the percentage of cardiac output supplied to kidney?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The kidneys receive approximately 20–22% of the cardiac output, despite making up only about 0.4% of body weight. This very high blood flow is necessary primarily for glomerular filtration and regulation of fluid and electrolyte balance.

  • Renal blood flow → ~21% of cardiac output ⭐

  • Approximately 1.0–1.2 L/min in a healthy adult at rest

  • Renal cortex receives the vast majority of renal blood flow.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Kidney → ~21% cardiac output

  • Brain → ~15%

  • Liver → ~25% (including portal flow)

  • Skeletal muscle → variable

Exam Pearl:
Kidneys receive ~20–22% of cardiac output → choose 21%.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৬) What is the most abundant component of surfactant?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Dipalmitoyl phosphatidylcholine (DPPC), also called dipalmitoyl lecithin, is the major and most abundant component of pulmonary surfactant. It is a phospholipid produced by type II pneumocytes and greatly reduces alveolar surface tension, preventing alveolar collapse, especially during expiration.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • DPPC → major component of surfactant ⭐

  • Produced by → Type II pneumocytes

  • Main function → ↓ alveolar surface tension

  • Prevents → atelectasis

  • Phosphatidylglycerol → smaller component but important marker of fetal lung maturity

Exam Pearl:
“DPPC = pulmonary surfactant’s major phospholipid.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৭) Average daily secretion of gastric juice..?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Explanation:
The average daily secretion of gastric juice is approximately 1.5 liters (1500 mL) per day in a healthy adult. Gastric juice contains HCl, pepsinogen, intrinsic factor, mucus, and water/electrolytes. Its acidic environment helps with protein digestion and provides a defense against ingested microorganisms.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gastric juice → ~1500 mL/day ⭐

  • HCl → secreted by parietal cells

  • Pepsinogen → chief cells

  • Intrinsic factor → parietal cells

  • Mucus → protects gastric mucosa

Exam Pearl:
Gastric juice secretion ≈ 1.5 L/day → 1500 mL.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৮) Autonomic bladder is caused by spinal cord damage above........region?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
An autonomic (reflex) bladder occurs when the spinal cord is damaged above the sacral micturition center (S2–S4). The sacral reflex arc remains intact, but voluntary control from higher centers is lost. As a result, the bladder can empty reflexly when sufficiently distended.

  • Lesion above S2–S4 → autonomic/reflex bladder ⭐

  • Lesion involving S2–S4 or pelvic nerves → atonic/flaccid bladder

  • Higher centers → provide voluntary control and inhibition of micturition

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Micturition center → S2–S4

  • Above S2–S4 lesion → reflex/autonomic bladder

  • S2–S4 lesion → atonic bladder

Exam Pearl:
“Above sacral center = reflex (autonomic) bladder.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৩৯) Which hormone acts on collecting tubule & duct?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
ADH (antidiuretic hormone/vasopressin) acts primarily on the late distal tubule and collecting tubules/ducts of the kidney. It increases water permeability by inserting aquaporin-2 channels into the apical membrane of principal cells, thereby increasing water reabsorption and concentrating urine.

  • ADH → collecting tubule/duct → ↑ water reabsorption ⭐

  • Aldosterone → mainly acts on late distal tubule and collecting duct → ↑ Na⁺ reabsorption, ↑ K⁺ secretion

  • ANP → promotes Na⁺ and water excretion

  • PTH → acts mainly on proximal tubule and distal tubule

Exam Pearl:
ADH = collecting duct = water reabsorption.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪০) Oxytocin is made up of up to....... Amino acids?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Oxytocin is a nonapeptide hormone, meaning it consists of 9 amino acids. It is synthesized in the hypothalamus, mainly in the paraventricular and supraoptic nuclei, and stored and released from the posterior pituitary.

  • Oxytocin → 9 amino acids ⭐

  • ADH (vasopressin) → also 9 amino acids

  • Insulin → 51 amino acids

  • Growth hormone → 191 amino acids

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Oxytocin → Nonapeptide → 9 aa

  • ADH → Nonapeptide → 9 aa

  • Insulin → 51 aa

  • GH → 191 aa

Exam Pearl:
Oxytocin = 9 amino acids = nonapeptide.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪১) Which gland is called the ‘life-saving gland’?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The adrenal gland is often called the “life-saving gland” because its hormones, particularly cortisol and aldosterone, are essential for maintaining blood pressure, fluid/electrolyte balance, metabolism, and the body's response to stress.

Complete absence of adrenal cortical hormones can lead to life-threatening adrenal insufficiency.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adrenal → “life-saving gland” 

  • Cortex → cortisol, aldosterone, adrenal androgens

  • Medulla → adrenaline & noradrenaline

  • Cortisol → stress response and vascular support

  • Aldosterone → Na⁺ retention and K⁺ excretion

Exam Pearl:
Adrenal gland = life-saving gland.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪২) Which one is male pill?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Gossypol is a compound derived from cottonseed that has been studied as a male contraceptive (“male pill”). It can suppress sperm production, producing reversible or sometimes prolonged infertility.

  • Gossypol → male contraceptive 

  • Cyclofem → injectable female hormonal contraceptive

  • Lippes loop → IUD

  • Norplant → subdermal contraceptive implant

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Male pill → Gossypol

  • Cyclofem → injectable hormonal contraception

  • Lippes loop → IUD

  • Norplant → implant

Exam Pearl:
Gossypol = classic exam answer for the “male pill.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৩) Which one has anti-inflammatory effect?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cortisol is a glucocorticoid produced by the zona fasciculata of the adrenal cortex. It has potent anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects, which is why glucocorticoids are widely used to treat inflammatory and autoimmune conditions.

  • Cortisol → anti-inflammatory ⭐

  • Aldosterone → sodium and water retention; potassium excretion

  • Androgens → sex-hormone effects

  • Epinephrine → cardiovascular and metabolic effects

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Cortisol → anti-inflammatory + immunosuppressive

  • Aldosterone → Na⁺ retention, K⁺ excretion

  • Adrenal androgens → secondary sexual characteristics

  • Epinephrine → fight-or-flight response

Exam Pearl:
“Cortisol calms inflammation.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৪) Which factor stimulates insulin secretion?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Acetylcholine (ACh) stimulates insulin secretion from pancreatic β-cells through muscarinic M3 receptors. This is part of the parasympathetic (“rest and digest”) response and helps promote insulin release during feeding.

In contrast, epinephrine and norepinephrine generally inhibit insulin secretion, particularly through α₂-adrenergic receptors. Somatostatin also inhibits insulin secretion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • ACh → ↑ Insulin secretion ⭐

  • Glucose → major physiological stimulus for insulin

  • β₂ stimulation → ↑ insulin

  • α₂ stimulation → ↓ insulin

  • Somatostatin → ↓ insulin

Exam Pearl:
ACh stimulates insulin; sympathetic α₂ activity inhibits insulin.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৫) What is primary sexual organ in male?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The testes are the primary sexual (reproductive) organs in males because they produce both spermatozoa and the male sex hormone testosterone.

  • Testes → primary male sexual organs ⭐

  • Penis → copulatory organ

  • Scrotum → protects and maintains temperature of testes

  • Epididymis → sperm maturation and storage

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Male primary sex organ → Testes

  • Female primary sex organ → Ovaries

  • Testes → sperm + testosterone

Exam Pearl:
Primary sex organs = gonads → Testes in males, ovaries in females.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৬) Which one is the most active adrenal androgen?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the adrenal androgens listed, androstenedione is generally considered more biologically active than DHEA. However, testosterone is the more potent androgen overall, but it is produced mainly by the testes in males rather than being the principal adrenal androgen.

  • DHEA → major adrenal androgen precursor

  • Androstenedione → more active adrenal androgen 

  • Testosterone → potent androgen, mainly gonadal

  • Cortisol → glucocorticoid, not an androgen

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Zona reticularis → DHEA + androstenedione

  • DHEA → major adrenal androgen precursor

  • Androstenedione → more active adrenal androgen

  • Testosterone → most potent androgen among these options

Exam Pearl:
For this MCQ, “most active adrenal androgen” → Androstenedione.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৭) What is the chemical nature of the hormone Thyroxine?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Thyroxine (T4) is an iodinated derivative of the amino acid tyrosine, so it is classified as an amino-acid/tyrosine derivative hormone, not a steroid or protein hormone.

It is synthesized in the thyroid follicular cells from tyrosine residues in thyroglobulin, with iodine incorporated into the molecule.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • T3 & T4 → Tyrosine derivatives 

  • Thyroid hormones contain iodine

  • Steroid hormones → derived from cholesterol

  • Protein/peptide hormones → e.g., insulin, GH

Exam Pearl:
T3/T4 = iodinated tyrosine derivatives.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৮) Which one is polysynaptic reflex arc?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The crossed extension reflex is a polysynaptic reflex because the sensory neuron connects to multiple interneurons before reaching the motor neurons. It typically accompanies the withdrawal reflex: when one limb withdraws from a painful stimulus, the opposite limb extends to maintain posture.

  • Stretch reflex → monosynaptic

  • Withdrawal reflex → polysynaptic

  • Crossed extension reflex → polysynaptic ⭐

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Stretch reflex → Monosynaptic

  • Withdrawal/flexor reflex → Polysynaptic

  • Crossed extension reflex → Polysynaptic

  • Crossed extension → maintains postural support

Exam Pearl:
If asked for a classic polysynaptic reflex, think withdrawal + crossed extension reflex.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৪৯) Which part of limbic system is concerned with converting recent memory to long term memory?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The hippocampus is the key part of the limbic system involved in consolidating recent/short-term memories into long-term memories. Damage to the hippocampus can cause severe difficulty forming new long-term memories (anterograde amnesia).

  • Hippocampus → memory consolidation ⭐

  • Cingulate gyrus → emotion, motivation, memory-related processing

  • Parahippocampal gyrus → memory and contextual processing

  • Amygdala → emotion, especially fear and emotional memory

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Recent → long-term memory → Hippocampus

  • Fear/emotional memory → Amygdala

  • Hippocampal damage → anterograde amnesia

Exam Pearl:
Hippocampus = consolidation of recent memories into long-term memory.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫০) Which sensation bypasses thalamus?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Olfaction (smell) is the classic sensory modality that bypasses the thalamus in its initial pathway to reach the primary olfactory cortex. Most other major sensory modalities relay through the thalamus before reaching their respective primary cortical areas.

  • Olfaction → bypasses thalamus initially ⭐

  • Vision → lateral geniculate nucleus (LGN)

  • Audition → medial geniculate nucleus (MGN)

  • Gustation → VPM nucleus of thalamus

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Smell → Olfactory pathway → no initial thalamic relay

  • Vision → LGN

  • Audition → MGN

  • Taste → VPM

Exam Pearl:
“Smell is the exception: olfaction bypasses the thalamus.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫১) The principal adaptive responses excludes........?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The principal adaptive responses of cells are:

  • Hypertrophy → increase in cell size

  • Hyperplasia → increase in cell number

  • Atrophy → decrease in cell size/number

  • Metaplasia → reversible change from one differentiated cell type to another

Anaplasia is not a normal cellular adaptation. It refers to loss of cellular differentiation, a characteristic feature of malignancy.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hypertrophy → ↑ cell size

  • Hyperplasia → ↑ cell number

  • Atrophy → ↓ cell size

  • Metaplasia → reversible change in cell type

  • Anaplasia → loss of differentiation → malignancy 

Exam Pearl:
Anaplasia = malignant cellular change, not adaptation.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫২) Where does Caseous necrosis occur?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Caseous necrosis is classically associated with tuberculosis (TB). It produces a soft, cheese-like appearance and is typically found within tuberculous granulomas.

  • TB → Caseous necrosis ⭐

  • Syphilis → classically gummatous necrosis

  • Lymphoma → not characteristically associated with caseous necrosis

  • Sarcoidosis → non-caseating granulomas

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Caseating granuloma → TB

  • Non-caseating granuloma → Sarcoidosis

  • Gummatous lesion → Tertiary syphilis

Exam Pearl:
“Caseous = TB” is a classic pathology association.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৩) Enzymes for free radical degradation excludes.....?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The major antioxidant enzymes responsible for degrading or detoxifying free radicals/reactive oxygen species (ROS) include:

  • Superoxide dismutase (SOD) → converts superoxide radicals (O₂⁻) to H₂O₂.

  • Catalase → converts H₂O₂ into water and oxygen.

  • Glutathione peroxidase → reduces H₂O₂ and lipid peroxides.

Myeloperoxidase (MPO) is different. It is found mainly in neutrophils and uses H₂O₂ to generate hypochlorous acid (HOCl) for microbial killing rather than serving as a primary antioxidant enzyme.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • SOD → O₂⁻ → H₂O₂

  • Catalase → H₂O₂ → H₂O + O₂

  • Glutathione peroxidase → H₂O₂/lipid peroxide → reduced products

  • MPO → HOCl formation → antimicrobial killing ⭐

Exam Pearl:
MPO generates ROS for killing; SOD, catalase, and glutathione peroxidase detoxify ROS.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৪) Virchow’s triad doesn’t include---?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Virchow’s triad describes the three major factors predisposing to thrombosis:

  1. Endothelial injury 

  2. Hypercoagulability 

  3. Alteration of normal blood flow (stasis or turbulence) 

Hypocoagulability means reduced blood clotting tendency, so it does not contribute to thrombus formation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Virchow's triad → Endothelial injury + abnormal blood flow + hypercoagulability

  • Abnormal blood flow → stasis/turbulence

  • Hypocoagulability → NOT included

Exam Pearl:
“3 Hs”: Hypercoagulability + Hemodynamic alteration + endothelial injury.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৫) How many stages of shock are there?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Shock is classically described in 3 stages:

  1. Compensated stage – the body maintains blood pressure and vital-organ perfusion through sympathetic and hormonal mechanisms.

  2. Progressive (decompensated) stage – tissue hypoperfusion worsens, causing metabolic acidosis and progressive circulatory failure.

  3. Irreversible (refractory) stage – severe cellular and organ damage develops, making recovery unlikely.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • 1st → Compensated

  • 2nd → Progressive

  • 3rd → Irreversible 

Exam Pearl:
Shock = 3 stages: Compensated → Progressive → Irreversible.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৬) Philadelphia chromosome is found in--?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The Philadelphia chromosome (t(9;22)(q34;q11)) is classically associated with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML). It results from a reciprocal translocation between chromosomes 9 and 22, creating the BCR-ABL1 fusion gene, which encodes a constitutively active tyrosine kinase.

It can also occur in a subset of ALL, especially adult B-cell ALL, but the classic association is CML.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Philadelphia chromosome → CML 

  • Translocation → t(9;22)

  • Fusion gene → BCR-ABL1

  • BCR-ABL1 → constitutive tyrosine kinase activity

  • Treatment → Imatinib and other BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors

Exam Pearl:
Philadelphia chromosome = CML = t(9;22) = BCR-ABL1.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৭) Which Tumor arises from more than one germ layer?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A teratoma is a tumor that arises from more than one germ layer—often all three embryonic germ layers: ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm. It may therefore contain tissues such as skin, cartilage, muscle, neural tissue, or glandular tissue.

  • Papilloma → benign epithelial tumor

  • Carcinoma → malignant epithelial tumor

  • Sarcoma → malignant mesenchymal/connective-tissue tumor

  • Teratoma → tissues from multiple germ layers 

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Teratoma → ≥2 germ layers

  • Mature teratoma → usually well-differentiated tissues

  • Germ cell tumor → common sites include ovary and testis

Exam Pearl:
“Teratoma = tumor containing tissues from multiple germ layers.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৮) How many types of hemorrhage are the according to duration of onset of hemorrhage?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
According to the duration/onset of hemorrhage, hemorrhage is classically divided into 3 types:

  1. Primary hemorrhage – occurs immediately after injury or during an operation.

  2. Reactionary hemorrhage – occurs within about 24 hours, often due to slipping of a ligature, rise in blood pressure, or loss of vasoconstriction.

  3. Secondary hemorrhage – occurs after 7 days or later, commonly due to infection and erosion of a blood vessel.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Primary → immediate

  • Reactionary → within 24 hours

  • Secondary → usually after ~7 days 

Exam Pearl:
Hemorrhage by onset = 3 types: Primary → Reactionary → Secondary.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৫৯) For the preservation of fresh tissue which formaldehyde preparation is used?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
For routine preservation of fresh tissue specimens, 10% formalin is commonly used. More precisely, 10% neutral buffered formalin (NBF) is the standard fixative in histopathology. It is approximately equivalent to 4% formaldehyde because commercial formalin is about 37–40% formaldehyde.

  • 10% formalin → routine tissue fixation/preservation 

  • 40% → concentrated formaldehyde stock solution, not used routinely

  • 90–99% → not a routine tissue fixative

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Routine tissue fixation → 10% neutral buffered formalin

  • 10% formalin ≈ 4% formaldehyde

  • Formalin → prevents autolysis and putrefaction

Exam Pearl:
Histopathology tissue fixation = 10% neutral buffered formalin.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬০) Subcutaneous hematoma measuring >1 cm is called..?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ecchymosis is a relatively large area of subcutaneous bleeding, typically >1 cm in diameter. It commonly appears as a bruise due to blood escaping from damaged small vessels into the tissues.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Petechiae → <2 mm

  • Purpura → ~2 mm–1 cm

  • Ecchymosis → >1 cm 

  • Skin rash → not a specific term for hemorrhage

Exam Pearl:
“>1 cm = Ecchymosis; 2 mm–1 cm = Purpura; <2 mm = Petechiae.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬১) Septic shock is characterized by following features, except..?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In septic shock, severe systemic infection triggers inflammatory mediators that cause widespread endothelial injury, systemic vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, and activation—not inactivation—of the coagulation system. Coagulation activation can lead to microvascular thrombosis and DIC. Respiratory distress, including ARDS, may also occur due to widespread inflammatory injury.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Septic shock → vasodilation + hypotension

  • Endothelial injury → ↑ vascular permeability

  • Coagulation → activated, may cause DIC 

  • Respiratory distress/ARDS → common complication

Exam Pearl:
Sepsis activates coagulation; it does not inactivate it.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬২) Which one is the most important cause of NGU?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Chlamydia trachomatis is the most important and most common cause of nongonococcal urethritis (NGU). It is an obligate intracellular bacterium and commonly causes urethral discharge, dysuria, and sometimes asymptomatic infection.

  • Chlamydia trachomatis → major cause of NGU ⭐

  • Ureaplasma urealyticum → can cause NGU, but is less commonly the classic exam answer

  • Trichomonas vaginalis → less common cause

  • HSV → uncommon cause of urethritis

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • NGU → Chlamydia trachomatis

  • Gonococcal urethritis → Neisseria gonorrhoeae

  • Chlamydia → obligate intracellular organism

  • Common presentation → dysuria + urethral discharge

Exam Pearl:
NGU = Chlamydia until proven otherwise (classic exam association).

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৩) Complication of falciparum malaria excludes..?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hyperglycemia is not a typical complication of Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Severe falciparum malaria can cause hypoglycemia, particularly due to increased glucose consumption by the parasite and quinine-induced hyperinsulinemia.

Important complications include:

  • Hyperpyrexia

  • Severe hemolytic anemia

  • Acute renal failure (ARF)

  • Cerebral malaria

  • Metabolic/lactic acidosis

  • Hypoglycemia

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Falciparum → Hypoglycemia 

  • → Severe anemia

  • → Cerebral malaria

  • → ARF

  • → Hyperpyrexia

Exam Pearl:
In severe falciparum malaria, think “hypoglycemia,” not hyperglycemia.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৪) In CBC report, what type of abnormality is found in ascariasis?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Ascariasis, caused by Ascaris lumbricoides, commonly produces eosinophilia, particularly during the larval migration phase through the lungs. Eosinophils are important in the immune response against helminthic parasites.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Helminthic infection → Eosinophilia 

  • Ascariasis → eosinophilia, especially during tissue migration

  • Bacterial infection → often neutrophilia

  • Viral infection → often lymphocytosis

Exam Pearl:
“Parasites → eosinophils.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৫) Which one is the causative factor for genital warts?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Genital warts (condyloma acuminata) are caused by Human papillomavirus (HPV), most commonly HPV types 6 and 11. These are considered low-risk HPV types because they are generally not associated with cervical cancer.

  • HPV → genital warts 

  • HSV → genital herpes

  • Treponema pallidum → syphilis

  • Neisseria gonorrhoeae → gonorrhea

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Genital warts → HPV 6, 11

  • Cervical cancer → mainly HPV 16, 18

  • Genital herpes → HSV-2 (classically)

  • Syphilis → T. pallidum

Exam Pearl:
“6 & 11 = warts; 16 & 18 = cancer.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৬) What type of hypersensitivity reaction occurs in anaphylactic shock?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Anaphylactic shock is a severe, systemic Type I (immediate) hypersensitivity reaction. It is mediated by IgE antibodies. On re-exposure to an allergen, IgE-bound mast cells and basophils rapidly degranulate, releasing histamine, leukotrienes, and other mediators, causing widespread vasodilation, increased vascular permeability, bronchoconstriction, and potentially severe hypotension.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Type I → IgE → anaphylaxis 

  • Type II → IgG/IgM against cell or tissue antigens

  • Type III → immune-complex mediated

  • Type IV → T-cell mediated, delayed

Exam Pearl:
Anaphylaxis = Type I hypersensitivity = IgE-mediated.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৭) Bone deformity occurs in which type of anemia?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Bone deformities are classically associated with thalassemia, particularly β-thalassemia major. Severe chronic anemia causes increased erythropoietic activity and expansion of the bone marrow, especially in the skull and facial bones. This produces characteristic features such as frontal bossing, maxillary hypertrophy, and “chipmunk facies.”

  • Aplastic anemia → bone marrow failure, no marrow expansion

  • Megaloblastic anemia → macrocytic anemia due to impaired DNA synthesis

  • Thalassemia → marrow expansion → bone deformity 

  • IDA → no characteristic bone deformity

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Thalassemia major → marrow expansion

  • Facial changes → frontal bossing + maxillary enlargement

  • Skull X-ray → “hair-on-end” appearance

Exam Pearl:
Thalassemia → chronic hemolysis → marrow expansion → bone deformity.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৮) Schilling test is done for the assessment of---?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The Schilling test is a classic test used to assess vitamin B12 absorption, particularly in evaluating the cause of vitamin B12 deficiency. It historically helped distinguish pernicious anemia (intrinsic-factor deficiency) from other causes of B12 malabsorption.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Schilling test → Vitamin B12 absorption 

  • Pernicious anemia → intrinsic factor deficiency

  • B12 deficiency → megaloblastic anemia + neurological manifestations

Exam Pearl:
Schilling test = B12 absorption test.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৬৯) What is the normal value of APTT?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
APTT (Activated Partial Thromboplastin Time) evaluates the intrinsic and common coagulation pathways. The normal value is approximately 30–40 seconds, although the exact reference range can vary slightly between laboratories.

  • APTT → Intrinsic + common pathway 

  • PT → Extrinsic + common pathway

  • APTT is prolonged in → Hemophilia, heparin therapy, intrinsic-factor deficiencies

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • APTT → 30–40 sec

  • PT → ~11–14 sec

  • Hemophilia → ↑ APTT, normal PT

  • Warfarin → ↑ PT/INR

  • Heparin → ↑ APTT

Exam Pearl:
APTT ≈ 30–40 seconds → intrinsic pathway.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭০) Granular yellowish colour sputum found in..?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Actinomycosis classically produces yellowish “sulfur granules” in the sputum. These are colonies of Actinomyces organisms and are an important diagnostic clue.

  • Actinomycosis → yellow sulfur granules in sputum 

  • Anthracosis → black pigmentation due to carbon deposition

  • Pseudomonas → classically greenish/blue-green sputum may occur

  • Pneumonia → purulent sputum, but sulfur granules are not characteristic

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Yellow sulfur granules → Actinomyces

  • Black sputum → anthracosis

  • Greenish sputum → Pseudomonas (classically described)

  • Rust-colored sputum → pneumococcal pneumonia

Exam Pearl:
“Sulfur granules = Actinomycosis.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭১) A granuloma surrounded by fibrous tissue that has undergone caseation necrosis, is called..?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A tubercle is the characteristic granulomatous lesion of tuberculosis. It consists of caseous necrosis surrounded by epithelioid cells, Langhans giant cells, and lymphocytes, and may become surrounded by fibrous tissue.

  • Ghon focus → a primary tuberculous focus in the lung.

  • Ghon complex → Ghon focus + involved regional hilar lymph nodes.

  • Tubercle → caseating granuloma characteristic of TB 

  • Hilar lymph node → regional lymph node, not the granuloma itself.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Caseating granuloma → Tubercle

  • Ghon focus → primary pulmonary focus

  • Ghon complex → Ghon focus + hilar lymph nodes

  • Langhans giant cells → TB granuloma

Exam Pearl:
“Caseating granuloma of TB = tubercle.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭২) Which of the following causes infection of prosthetic heart bulb & hip?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Staphylococcus epidermidis is a common cause of prosthetic device infections, including prosthetic heart valves and prosthetic joints (e.g., hip). Its key virulence factor is biofilm formation, which allows it to adhere to artificial surfaces and resist host defenses and antibiotics.

  • S. epidermidis → prosthetic devices 

  • S. aureus → skin/soft-tissue infections, bacteremia, endocarditis, osteomyelitis

  • S. saprophyticus → urinary tract infection, especially in young women

  • S. pyogenes → pharyngitis, cellulitis, necrotizing fasciitis

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Prosthetic valve/joint → S. epidermidis

  • Biofilm/slime layer → S. epidermidis

  • UTI → S. saprophyticus

  • Acute infective endocarditis → S. aureus

Exam Pearl:
“Prosthetic material + biofilm = S. epidermidis.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৩) What is the usual site of latency for CMV?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cytomegalovirus (CMV) establishes lifelong latency mainly in cells of the monocyte/macrophage lineage, including myeloid progenitor cells. Reactivation can occur when cellular immunity is suppressed, particularly in transplant recipients and other immunocompromised patients.

  • CMV → monocytes/myeloid lineage 

  • Cranial sensory ganglia → classically HSV/VZV latency

  • B lymphocytes → EBV latency

  • Lumbar sensory ganglia → not the usual CMV site

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CMV → Monocytes/myeloid cells

  • EBV → B lymphocytes

  • HSV-1 → Trigeminal ganglion

  • VZV → Dorsal root/sensory ganglia

Exam Pearl:
“CMV hides in monocytes.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৪) Which one is most important antiphagocytic factor S. Pyogenes?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The M protein is the most important antiphagocytic virulence factor of Streptococcus pyogenes. It is located on the bacterial surface and interferes with opsonization and phagocytosis, particularly by inhibiting complement-mediated clearance.

  • M protein → antiphagocytic 

  • DNase → breaks down DNA in pus

  • Hyaluronidase → facilitates tissue spread

  • Streptokinase → dissolves fibrin and promotes spread

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • S. pyogenes → M protein = antiphagocytic

  • Streptolysin O → cytolytic, oxygen-labile

  • Streptokinase → fibrinolysis

  • Hyaluronidase → “spreading factor”

  • DNase → liquefies pus

Exam Pearl:
M protein is the major antiphagocytic factor of S. pyogenes.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৫) What is the shape of capsid of rabies virus?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The rabies virus has a characteristic bullet-shaped capsid/virion. It belongs to the family Rhabdoviridae and genus Lyssavirus.

  • Rabies virus → Bullet-shaped 

  • Influenza virus → roughly spherical/pleomorphic

  • Adenovirus → icosahedral

  • Poxvirus → complex/brick-shaped

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Rabies → Bullet-shaped

  • Family → Rhabdoviridae

  • Genus → Lyssavirus

  • Genome → negative-sense ssRNA

Exam Pearl:
“Rabies = bullet-shaped virus.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৬) Treatment duration of severe case of extrapulmonary TB is..?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
For severe extrapulmonary tuberculosis (TB) involving sites such as the CNS (TB meningitis) or bone/joint, treatment is generally extended beyond the standard 6-month regimen. In many exam-oriented guidelines, 12 months is the expected duration for severe extrapulmonary TB, particularly TB meningitis.

  • Pulmonary TB → commonly 6 months

  • Severe extrapulmonary TB → 12 months ⭐

  • TB meningitis → often 9–12 months, depending on guideline

  • Bone/joint TB → may require 9–12 months

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Standard TB → 6 months

  • Severe EPTB → 12 months

  • TB meningitis → 9–12 months

  • Bone/joint TB → prolonged therapy

Exam Pearl:
Severe extrapulmonary TB → think 12 months.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৭) Which one is the most important diagnostic method in enteric fever?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Blood culture is the most important and preferred diagnostic test for enteric (typhoid) fever, especially during the first week of illness. It directly demonstrates Salmonella Typhi or S. Paratyphi and allows antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

  • Blood culture → best diagnostic test ⭐

  • Widal test → less reliable; supportive rather than definitive

  • Urine culture → lower sensitivity

  • CBC → nonspecific findings such as leukopenia may occur

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Enteric fever → Blood culture

  • Best yield → early in illness

  • Widal → limited specificity/sensitivity

  • Bone marrow culture → most sensitive, but not routinely used

Exam Pearl:
Suspected typhoid → take blood culture before antibiotics whenever possible.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৮) Which has association with HLA-B27?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
HLA-B27 is strongly associated with the group of seronegative spondyloarthropathies, particularly ankylosing spondylitis. These disorders characteristically involve the axial skeleton and entheses and are usually RF-negative.

Examples include:

  • Ankylosing spondylitis ⭐

  • Reactive arthritis

  • Psoriatic arthritis

  • Enteropathic arthritis

  • Some forms of juvenile spondyloarthritis

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HLA-B27 → Seronegative spondyloarthropathies

  • Strongest classic association → Ankylosing spondylitis

  • RA → associated with HLA-DR4

  • SLE → associated with HLA-DR2/DR3

Exam Pearl:
HLA-B27 = Ankylosing spondylitis = seronegative spondyloarthropathy.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৯) Which of the following is not a pattern of angina?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The major clinical patterns of angina pectoris include:

  • Stable angina → predictable with exertion, relieved by rest.

  • Unstable angina → new, worsening, or occurring at rest; an acute coronary syndrome.

  • Prinzmetal (variant) angina → caused by transient coronary artery spasm, usually occurring at rest.

Paroxysmal angina is not a standard recognized pattern/classification of angina pectoris in this context.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Stable → exertional

  • Unstable → ACS / unpredictable

  • Prinzmetal → coronary vasospasm, usually at rest

  • Paroxysmal → not a standard angina pattern ⭐

Exam Pearl:
Three classic patterns: Stable, Unstable, and Prinzmetal (variant).

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮০) Which one is tumor of heart?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Cardiac myxoma is the most common primary benign tumor of the heart. It most commonly arises in the left atrium, usually attached to the interatrial septum near the fossa ovalis.

  • Myxoma → cardiac tumor 

  • Mesothelioma → tumor of mesothelial tissue, commonly pleura/pericardium

  • Hamartoma → benign developmental malformation-like lesion

  • Cardioma → not a standard specific cardiac tumor

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common primary cardiac tumor → Myxoma

  • Most common location → Left atrium

  • Common attachment → Interatrial septum

  • Can produce → obstructive, embolic, and constitutional symptoms

Exam Pearl:
“Left atrial mass + tumor symptoms = think cardiac myxoma.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮১) Which form of anemia is common in strict vegetarians?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Strict vegetarians are at risk of vitamin B12 deficiency because vitamin B12 is found predominantly in animal-derived foods. B12 deficiency impairs DNA synthesis and causes megaloblastic anemia, characterized by large, abnormal red blood cell precursors.

  • Strict vegetarian → Vitamin B12 deficiency → Megaloblastic anemia 

  • Hemolytic → increased RBC destruction

  • Microcytic → commonly iron deficiency

  • Normocytic → many causes, including acute blood loss

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • B12 deficiency → Megaloblastic anemia

  • Folate deficiency → Megaloblastic anemia

  • B12 deficiency → neurological manifestations may occur

  • Strict vegan diet → risk of B12 deficiency

Exam Pearl:
“Strict vegetarian + megaloblastic anemia → think vitamin B12 deficiency.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮২) Pitting oedema occurs in following all of the condition except.....?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pitting edema occurs when excess fluid accumulates in the interstitial space and can be displaced by pressure. It is commonly seen in:

  • Heart failure (HF) → increased hydrostatic pressure

  • Nephrotic syndrome (NS) → hypoalbuminemia → reduced oncotic pressure

  • Cirrhosis → hypoalbuminemia + portal hypertension

Lymphatic obstruction, however, typically causes non-pitting edema (lymphedema) because protein-rich fluid accumulates in the tissues and becomes progressively fibrotic.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HF → Pitting edema

  • Nephrotic syndrome → Pitting edema

  • Cirrhosis → Pitting edema

  • Lymphatic obstruction → Non-pitting edema 

Exam Pearl:
“Lymphedema = non-pitting edema.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৩) What is the cause of differential clubbing?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Differential clubbing is classically associated with PDA (patent ductus arteriosus) with pulmonary hypertension and right-to-left shunting. Deoxygenated blood enters the descending aorta distal to the branches supplying the upper limbs. Therefore, the lower limbs become cyanotic and clubbed, while the upper limbs remain relatively normal.

  • PDA + pulmonary hypertension → differential cyanosis + clubbing ⭐

  • TOF → usually generalized cyanosis/clubbing, not differential

  • VSD → not classically associated

  • ASD → not classically associated

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Differential clubbing → PDA with pulmonary hypertension

  • Upper limbs → relatively spared

  • Lower limbs → cyanosis + clubbing

  • Mechanism → right-to-left shunt through PDA

Exam Pearl:
“Differential clubbing = PDA + pulmonary hypertension.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৪) What do we get from Drinking water?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fluoride is an important mineral obtained from drinking water, particularly fluoridated water. It helps strengthen tooth enamel and reduces the risk of dental caries.

  • Fluoride → drinking water 

  • Selenium → mainly obtained from foods such as seafood, meat, eggs, and cereals

  • Zinc → meat, seafood, legumes, nuts

  • Iodine → iodized salt, seafood, dairy products

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Drinking water → Fluoride

  • Iodized salt → Iodine

  • Seafood → iodine + selenium

  • Zinc → meat/seafood

Exam Pearl:
“Water → Fluoride → protects teeth from dental caries.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৫) Vertigo in older patients is most commonly due to....?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In older adults, the most common cause of true vertigo is benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV). It results from displacement of otoconia (calcium carbonate crystals) into the semicircular canals, most commonly the posterior canal. Head movement causes brief episodes of spinning sensation.

  • BPPV → most common cause of vertigo in older adults 

  • Cerebellopontine angle lesion → uncommon

  • Dementia → not a typical cause of vertigo

  • Vestibular neuronitis → usually acute, often following viral infection

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Elderly + brief positional vertigo → BPPV

  • Common canal → posterior semicircular canal

  • Cause → displaced otoconia

  • Diagnostic test → Dix–Hallpike test

Exam Pearl:
Older patient + vertigo triggered by head position = BPPV.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৬) Which is non-modifiable risk factor of coronary artery disease?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Male sex is a non-modifiable risk factor for coronary artery disease (CAD). It cannot be changed, unlike hypertension, smoking, and diabetes mellitus, which are modifiable or controllable risk factors.

Men generally develop CAD at a younger age than women, although the risk in women increases substantially after menopause.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Non-modifiable → Male sex, age, family history/genetics 

  • Hypertension → modifiable

  • Smoking → modifiable

  • Diabetes mellitus → modifiable

Exam Pearl:
CAD non-modifiable risk factors = age + male sex + family history.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৭) ACE inhibitors are contraindicated in...?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
ACE inhibitors such as enalapril and lisinopril are actually beneficial in diabetes and chronic kidney disease (CKD/CRF), particularly when albuminuria/proteinuria is present, because they reduce intraglomerular pressure and slow renal disease progression. They can also be used in PVD and COPD.

However, ACE inhibitors can cause a rise in creatinine and are contraindicated in bilateral renal artery stenosis, and should generally be avoided in pregnancy.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bilateral renal artery stenosis → ACEI contraindicated 

  • Pregnancy → contraindicated

  • Diabetes with albuminuria → often beneficial

  • CKD with proteinuria → often renoprotective

  • Common adverse effect → dry cough

  • Serious adverse effect → angioedema

Exam Pearl:
If forced to choose from DM, CRF, PVD, COPD, none is the correct contraindication.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৮) Hospital acquired pneumonia is called.........?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hospital-acquired pneumonia (HAP) is also called nosocomial pneumonia. It develops 48 hours or more after hospital admission and was not present or incubating at the time of admission.

  • HAP → Nosocomial pneumonia ⭐

  • CAP → Community-acquired pneumonia

  • Aspiration pneumonia → occurs after aspiration of gastric/oropharyngeal contents

  • Suppurative pneumonia → describes a type of inflammatory lung infection, not specifically hospital-acquired

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hospital-acquired → Nosocomial

  • Community-acquired → CAP

  • Ventilator-associated pneumonia → VAP

  • HAP typically develops ≥48 hours after admission

Exam Pearl:
Hospital-acquired pneumonia = Nosocomial pneumonia.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৯) Which anti TB drug causes hyperuricemia?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pyrazinamide (PZA) commonly causes hyperuricemia by reducing renal excretion of uric acid. This can precipitate gout or arthralgia, especially during prolonged treatment.

  • Pyrazinamide → Hyperuricemia ⭐

  • INH → peripheral neuropathy, hepatotoxicity

  • Rifampicin → hepatotoxicity, orange-red body fluids

  • Ethambutol → optic neuritis, red-green color blindness

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PZA → Hyperuricemia

  • INH → Peripheral neuropathy

  • Rifampicin → Orange body fluids

  • Ethambutol → Optic neuritis

Exam Pearl:
“PZA raises uric acid.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯০) What is the cause of recurrent & severe acute pancreatitis?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hereditary pancreatitis is classically associated with recurrent episodes of severe acute pancreatitis, often beginning at a young age and potentially progressing to chronic pancreatitis. It is commonly related to mutations such as PRSS1.

  • Hereditary pancreatitis → recurrent + severe acute attacks ⭐

  • Alcohol → major cause of acute and chronic pancreatitis, but not the classic answer for recurrent severe attacks in this MCQ

  • Tobacco → important risk factor, particularly for chronic pancreatitis

  • Post-necrotic → can cause chronic structural changes but is not the classic cause here

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Recurrent severe pancreatitis → Hereditary pancreatitis

  • PRSS1 mutation → hereditary pancreatitis

  • Alcohol → common acquired cause

  • Hereditary pancreatitis → increased risk of pancreatic carcinoma

Exam Pearl:
Young patient + recurrent severe pancreatitis + family history → think hereditary pancreatitis (PRSS1).

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯১) PUD is closely associated with......?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Peptic ulcer disease (PUD) is closely associated with Helicobacter pylori infection. H. pylori colonizes the gastric mucosa and contributes to mucosal injury through chronic inflammation, impaired mucosal defenses, and altered gastric acid regulation. It is an important cause of duodenal and gastric ulcers.

  • H. pylori → PUD ⭐

  • C. jejuni → gastroenteritis

  • E. coli → various intestinal infections

  • B. coli (Balantidium coli) → intestinal protozoal infection

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • PUD → H. pylori + NSAIDs

  • Duodenal ulcer → strongly associated with H. pylori

  • Gastric ulcer → H. pylori and NSAIDs

  • H. pylori → urease-positive organism

Exam Pearl:
PUD + chronic gastritis → think H. pylori.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯২) What is the cause of euvolemic hypernatremia?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Euvolemic hypernatremia occurs when there is a loss of free water without significant loss of sodium. The classic cause is diabetes insipidus (DI), due to deficiency of ADH (central DI) or resistance to ADH (nephrogenic DI). Water loss through the kidneys increases serum sodium concentration, while thirst and water intake may partially compensate for the volume loss.

  • Diabetes insipidus → euvolemic hypernatremia ⭐

  • Diuretic therapy → usually causes volume depletion and can produce hypovolemia

  • Glycosuria → osmotic diuresis, typically causing volume depletion

  • CRF → can cause various electrolyte abnormalities, but is not the classic answer

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Euvolemic hypernatremia → Diabetes insipidus

  • Hypovolemic hypernatremia → GI loss, sweating, diuretics

  • Hypervolemic hypernatremia → hypertonic saline/mineralocorticoid excess

  • DI → free-water loss

Exam Pearl:
“Hypernatremia + normal volume status = think Diabetes insipidus.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৩) What is absolute contraindication of stomach wash?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Corrosive poisoning (strong acids or alkalis) is an absolute contraindication to gastric lavage (stomach wash) because lavage can cause re-exposure of the esophagus and stomach to the corrosive substance, worsening mucosal injury and increasing the risk of perforation and aspiration.

  • Corrosive poisoning → gastric lavage contraindicated ⭐

  • OPC poisoning → gastric lavage may be considered with appropriate airway protection

  • Sedative poisoning → may be considered in selected cases, especially early and with a protected airway

  • Arsenic poisoning → gastric decontamination may be considered depending on circumstances

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Corrosives → NO gastric lavage

  • Hydrocarbons → generally avoid lavage due to aspiration risk

  • Unprotected airway → avoid lavage

  • Gastric lavage is not routinely recommended for most poisonings

Exam Pearl:
“Corrosive ingestion → never wash the stomach.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৪) Which is not an early complication of drowning?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Dehydration is not an early complication of drowning. Drowning primarily causes respiratory impairment and hypoxia due to aspiration of fluid and pulmonary injury.

Early complications can include:

  • Diffuse pulmonary edema 

  • Hypotension due to hypoxia and cardiovascular compromise

  • Hemoptysis due to pulmonary injury/alveolar damage

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Drowning → hypoxia is the key problem

  • Pulmonary edema → common early complication

  • Hypotension → may occur

  • Hemoptysis → may occur

  • Dehydration → not an early complication 

Exam Pearl:
Drowning = hypoxia + pulmonary edema, not dehydration.

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৫) Which one is not a feature of hyperthyroidism?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hyperthyroidism causes an increased metabolic rate, so patients typically experience weight loss despite increased appetite. Therefore, weight gain is not a typical feature.

Typical features include:

  • Excitability / nervousness 

  • Heat intolerance

  • Weight loss

  • Muscle weakness

  • Palpitations and tachycardia

  • Increased sweating

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Hyperthyroidism → Weight loss + heat intolerance + increased activity

  • Hypothyroidism → Weight gain + cold intolerance + lethargy

  • Hyperthyroidism → tremor, tachycardia, sweating

Exam Pearl:
Hyperthyroidism = “hot, thin, fast”; hypothyroidism = “cold, fat, slow.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৬) What is the first investigation to be done in stroke patient?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The first investigation in an acute stroke patient is a non-contrast CT scan of the brain. It is rapid and primarily used to distinguish ischemic stroke from intracranial hemorrhage, which is critical before giving thrombolytic therapy.

  • Non-contrast CT → first-line investigation 

  • MRI → more sensitive for early ischemic changes but usually not the initial emergency test

  • LP → not routinely done initially; may be considered in selected cases

  • DSA → used for vascular imaging/intervention in selected patients

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Acute stroke → Urgent non-contrast CT brain

  • CT shows hemorrhage quickly

  • Ischemic stroke → CT may initially be normal

  • MRI-DWI → highly sensitive for early ischemia

Exam Pearl:
“Stroke first → CT brain (non-contrast).”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৭) Which is the most common cause of dementia?
Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Alzheimer’s disease is the most common cause of dementia, accounting for the largest proportion of dementia cases. It is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by cognitive decline, memory impairment, and eventual loss of functional independence.

  • Alzheimer’s disease → most common cause of dementia ⭐

  • Cerebral tumor → can cause cognitive changes but is uncommon as a cause of dementia

  • Multiple sclerosis → may cause cognitive impairment but is not the commonest cause

  • Thiamine deficiency → classically causes Wernicke encephalopathy/Korsakoff syndrome

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common dementia → Alzheimer’s disease

  • Alzheimer’s → progressive memory loss + cognitive decline

  • Vascular dementia → commonly considered the second most common cause

  • Thiamine deficiency → Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome

Exam Pearl:
“Most common dementia = Alzheimer’s disease.”

Final Model Test-10 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৮) Which is the key feature of cardiovascular syphilis?

  • Adalimumab → anti-TNF-α monoclonal antibody

  • Rituximab → anti-CD20, not anti-TNF ⭐

  • Anti-TNF → Etanercept, Infliximab, Adalimumab

  • Anti-CD20 → Rituximab

  • Anti-IL-6 receptor → Tocilizumab

  • CTLA-4 Ig → Abatacept

Exam Pearl:
“Rituximab = CD20, not TNF.”
